summary: NASA has awarded SpaceX three additional crewed missions to the International Space Station as the agency prepares for the provider's 35th cargo resupply launch. In military space operations, U.S. Space Force leadership outlined a strategic blueprint to more than double the service's size over the next five years and announced plans to prototype new software fusing commercial and defense space-tracking data. Meanwhile, the Pentagon selected two companies for a reconnaissance satellite demonstration, and at least 134 personnel previously discharged under the COVID-19 vaccine mandate have returned to duty within the Air Force and Space Force. Internationally, France warned of heightened conflict risks in outer space in its 2035 national security plan, while European space-tracking initiatives reported expanding support. The commercial space sector logged substantial funding gains, led by Impulse Space raising $308 million in a Series D extension and EnduroSat securing $205 million, as Space Cargo Unlimited booked one-third of its Starfall capacity. In space technology, Icarus Robotics completed parabolic flight testing for its robotic system ahead of a planned flight to the space station. Scientific developments include a NASA spacecraft discovering a large new crater on the Moon, the joint NASA-JAXA XRISM mission observing a pulsar capturing stellar wind from a companion star, and the Hubble Space Telescope detailing an out-of-sync galaxy. Looking ahead, observers should watch for Albania's upcoming official signing ceremony to join NASA's Artemis Accords.
